title: What If You Stood on Mercury at Noon?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Mercury at noon? The scary part isn't only the heat.
By day, the surface reaches about 430 degrees Celsius, around 800 Fahrenheit.
Mercury has no true atmosphere, only a thin exosphere, so nothing holds that heat in after dark.
At night the ground plunges to about minus 180 Celsius. That's a swing of more than 600 degrees.
And the days are long. Sunrise to sunrise on Mercury takes 176 Earth days.
That's twice its 88-day year. By the time the Sun set, Mercury would have circled it once.
